themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints spiked to 147 this week versus a 78.9-week average—an 86% surge—signaling a potential new disturbance pattern or enforcement gap in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill.
evidence: 147 residential noise complaints this week vs. 78.9-week average (86% spike, z-score: 4.06)
Residential noise is among top 3 complaint categories overall (1,185 complaints over 90 days)
Spike is acute and concentrated in current week, not gradual
reporting_angles: Interview residents about what changed this week—new venue, construction, or events?
Check NYPD noise enforcement logs and response times for the district

themes_detail.label: Illegal Cannabis Retail Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 15 last week from a 3.6-week average—a 314% spike—suggesting rapid proliferation of unlicensed dispensaries in the district.
evidence: 15 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 3.6-week average (314% increase, z-score: 5.89)
First major spike in this complaint category suggests emerging problem, not baseline activity
Correlates with citywide illegal dispensary enforcement patterns
reporting_angles: Map the locations of complaints to identify retail cluster hot spots
Interview NYC Department of Consumer Affairs and police about enforcement strategy
Talk to block associations about community concerns beyond 311

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints exploded to 4 last week from near-zero (0.2-week average)—a 1,500% spike with a z-score of 8.66—indicating a severe and sudden waste management breakdown.
evidence: 4 commercial disposal complaints last week vs. 0.2-week average (1,500% spike, z-score: 8.66, severity: high)
Highest z-score among all current spikes indicates statistically extreme deviation
Suggests acute event or service disruption rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to identify service disruptions or contractor failures
Interview commercial business owners (restaurants, retail) about disposal costs and access
Check if specific waste hauler or area is affected

themes_detail.label: Air Quality & Environmental Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked 357% last week to 8 from a 1.8-week average, coinciding with potential industrial activity or emissions in the district.
evidence: 8 air quality complaints last week vs. 1.8-week average (357% spike, z-score: 3.81)
Unusual for this district—suggests new source or acute event
Correlates with commercial disposal spike, indicating possible broader sanitation/industrial issue
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with EPA air quality data and NYC DEP monitoring stations
Investigate whether industrial or construction activity ramped up recently
Interview residents about odors and health impacts

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise & Panhandling Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise jumped 210% three weeks ago (19 complaints vs. 6.1-week average), while panhandling complaints surged 1,100% two weeks ago (3 vs. 0.2-week average), suggesting growing street disorder and enforcement gaps.
evidence: 19 commercial noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.1-week average (210% spike, z-score: 5.7)
3 panhandling complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2-week average (1,100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Both spikes point to street-level disorder and potential homelessness/mental health nexus—aligns with CB budget requests for mental health de-stigmatization programs
reporting_angles: Interview business owners on main commercial corridors about disturbances
Connect panhandling spike to broader homelessness and mental health services in Queens
Examine police response and outreach coordination
